about.title: About FDN
about.metaDescription: FDN helps you decide what to eat in Hyderabad: dish-first rankings, living restaurant facts and honest community opinions.
about.intro: FDN is a food discovery network for Hyderabad. It answers one question fast: what should I eat, and where?
about.dishFirstBody: Restaurants are ranked by their dishes. Every restaurant page leads with what to order there, and every dish page ranks every place in the city that serves it.
about.factsBody: Opening hours, prices and phone numbers show when they were last confirmed. Anyone signed in can tap “Still true?” to keep them current.
about.honestBody: Ratings are weighted by trust, sponsored or hosted meals are labelled and never counted, and nothing paid can change a ranking, a dish score or a battle.
about.guestBody: You can browse, search, get directions and share without signing up. An account is only needed to rate, post, comment or vote.

guidelines.title: Community guidelines
guidelines.metaDescription: How FDN ratings work, what to disclose, what we remove and how to appeal.
guidelines.intro: FDN only works if people can trust what they read. These rules apply to every rating, post, comment, photo and fact.
guidelines.beHonestBody: Rate dishes you actually tried. Loved, Good, Okay and Skip describe the dish, not the restaurant’s staff or your mood that day.
guidelines.discloseBody: If the meal was free, paid for, or you work at or own the place, choose the matching disclosure. Disclosed posts stay visible with a tag, and their ratings are never counted in scores.
guidelines.scoresBody: Each rating is weighted by the member’s trust level and how recent it is. Scores are pulled toward the city average until enough ratings exist, and a score is shown only after at least three weighted ratings.
guidelines.removeItems: Spam and undisclosed promotion · Harassment, hate or threats · Sexual or violent content · Personal data such as private phone numbers or home addresses · Photos unrelated to food or restaurants · Fake or coordinated ratings
guidelines.enforcementBody: Moderators can remove content, lock threads, warn, suspend or ban. Three strikes in 90 days lead to an automatic 7-day suspension. Every action is recorded and the author is told why.
guidelines.appealBody: You can appeal each moderation action once. Appeals are reviewed by the FDN team, not by the moderator who acted.
